description: The Population Estimates Program (PEP) of the U.S. Census Bureau produces annual estimates of the resident population for the nation, states, metropolitan and micropolitan areas, counties, cities and towns, and for Puerto Rico and its municipios, together with housing unit estimates for the nation, states and counties. It also provides the components of population change (births, deaths, domestic and international migration) at national, state and county level, and population by age, sex, race and Hispanic origin. Each vintage (for example Vintage 2025) is a time series from the last decennial census to 1 July of the vintage year, revised from the census base with new administrative records; the latest vintage supersedes all earlier ones. Products are released between December and June; intercensal estimates revise each past decade. Access: CSV and XLSX downloads, past vintages on the FTP2 site, and some historical vintages through the Census Data API (the page notes that current estimates are not supported by the API); free and public domain. The Housing Unit Change Viewer maps housing unit change from 2020. Caveats: estimates are modelled, not counted; housing units are estimated only to county level and small-place estimates can be revised substantially. Simulation uses: annual updates of population and housing stock between censuses for exposure, demand growth and capacity planning. Related records: the 2020 Census DHC (the base), national population projections, the Building Permits Survey (an input to housing unit estimates) and the Community Resilience Estimates, which are modelled on PEP totals.
